---
title: Your first plugin in 5 minutes
description: Write a PLUGIN.md plugin with one tool, test it against recorded responses, and share it as a link. Worked example - the free-classrooms plugin.
icon: Rocket
---

This walks through a real plugin, [`plugins/classrooms`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins/tree/main/plugins/classrooms)
in the plugins repo, cut down to its smallest tool: **how many classrooms are free in each
teaching building right now**. It calls one public campus endpoint, so it needs no login.

Full language reference: [Declarative plugins](/docs/build/declarative-plugins) and the spec
[`PLUGIN-LANGUAGE.md`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness/blob/master/docs/PLUGIN-LANGUAGE.md).

<Steps>

<Step>

### Get the author CLI

The CLI lives in the plugins repo (bun required):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins
cd pku-harness-plugins
bun install
```

Usage: `bun run plugin validate|test|run <plugin-dir> [tool] [json-input]`.

</Step>

<Step>

### Write `PLUGIN.md`

One folder per plugin. The frontmatter is the manifest; the Markdown body is what the agent reads
about when and how to use your tools.

```md title="my-classrooms/PLUGIN.md"
---
spec: 1
id: my-classrooms
name: 教室概况
description: 各教学楼现在有多少空闲教室。
version: 0.1.0
author: your-github-name
network: [portal.pku.edu.cn]
tools:
  overview: tools/overview.yaml
i18n:
  en:
    name: Classroom overview
    description: How many classrooms are free in each teaching building right now.
---

my-classrooms__overview：各楼现在空闲教室数量。用户想找自习的地方时先用它挑楼。
```

- `network` lists every public host the plugin may call. Requests to anything else fail.
- Every file the app loads is named in the frontmatter. The app never lists folders, so any static
  host works.

</Step>

<Step>

### Write the tool

```yaml title="my-classrooms/tools/overview.yaml"
title: 各楼空闲教室数
description: 'How many classrooms are free right now in each teaching building: building, free, total.'
effect: read
steps:
  - let: r
    request:
      url: https://portal.pku.edu.cn/publicQuery/classroomQuery/retrClassRoomInfos.do
      headers: { referer: 'https://portal.pku.edu.cn/publicQuery/', accept: 'application/json' }
    as: json
  - check: "r.success && isList(r.rows)"
    error: 教室概况查询未成功
return: |
  {
    buildings: r.rows.map(b => ({ building: b.buildingName, free: b.classroomFree, total: b.classroomSum })),
  }
```

- `title` is shown to users (Chinese first); `description` is for the model.
- `effect` is `read`, `write`, `money` or `public`. Users choose per effect whether the agent may
  act on its own, so declare it honestly.
- Return data, never instructions. The result is shown to the model as data.

<Callout type="warn" title="YAML gotcha">
  Quote any expression or `${…}` template that contains `: ` or starts with `{` or `[`.
  Unquoted, YAML parses it as a map or a list. `validate` prints this hint when it happens.
</Callout>

</Step>

<Step>

### Record a test

Tests replay recorded responses, so they run offline and stay deterministic. Paste a (trimmed)
real response as the `body`, or save it as a file next to the test and use `file:`:

```yaml title="my-classrooms/tests/overview.yaml"
tool: overview
responses:
  - match: retrClassRoomInfos.do
    headers: { content-type: application/json }
    body: '{"success":true,"rows":[{"buildingName":"一教","classroomFree":16,"classroomSum":32}]}'
expect: { buildings: [{ building: 一教, free: 16, total: 32 }] }
```

A test has `tool`, optional `input` and `now`, the `responses` to serve (`match` a URL substring;
`body` or `file`; `campus` for campus requests), and either `expect` (compared **exactly** with
the result) or `expectError` (a pattern the error message must match).

</Step>

<Step>

### Validate, test, run

```bash
bun run plugin validate path/to/my-classrooms
bun run plugin test path/to/my-classrooms
bun run plugin run path/to/my-classrooms overview '{}'
```

`validate` checks the manifest, tool schemas, expressions and file paths, the same checks the app
and the marketplace run. `run` makes the real requests (public hosts only; campus requests need
the app, so record those in tests).

</Step>

<Step>

### Share it

Push the folder to a public GitHub repo. The folder URL is the install link:

```
https://github.com/<you>/<repo>/tree/main/my-classrooms
```

Students paste it in the app, scan its QR code, or open
`pkuharness://plugin?src=<url-encoded link>`. The app shows a review sheet first: community or
official, the websites it can reach (here `portal.pku.edu.cn`) and each tool with its effect.
Every `git push` becomes an update. To list it in the marketplace,
[submit the repo](/marketplace/submit). One repo can hold any number of plugins. See
[Publishing](/docs/marketplace/publishing).

</Step>

</Steps>
